Le Soleil, les planètes, la Lune et les: The Sun, the planets, the Moon and small bodies.
Huit planètes : Mercure, Vénus, Terre, M: Eight planets: Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars (rocky), Jupiter, Saturn (gas giants), Uranus, Neptune (ice giants).

La Terre est au plus près du Soleil débu: The Earth is closest to the Sun in early January, in the middle of the northern winter.
axe incliné de 23,4°, toujours dans la m: axis tilted 23.4°, always in the same direction
La Terre en juin et en décembre, axe tou: The Earth in June and in December, axis always tilted the same way
Comment les étoiles brillent, vivent et: How stars shine, live and die.
Une étoile brille par fusion nucléaire d: A star shines through nuclear fusion of hydrogen into helium in its core.
Sa couleur indique sa température : bleu: Its color shows its temperature: blue is very hot, red cooler.
Le Soleil deviendra une géante rouge pui: The Sun will become a red giant and then a white dwarf; massive stars end as supernovas.
Les éléments plus lourds que le fer se f: Elements heavier than iron form mostly in supernovas and neutron star mergers.
Les étoiles rouges ne sont pas les plus: Red stars are not the hottest: it's the opposite of faucets.
Couleur des étoiles selon leur températu: Color of stars according to their temperature
Les lois de Kepler, les satellites, les: Kepler's laws, satellites, tides, black holes.
Kepler 1 : les planètes décrivent des el: Kepler 1: planets move in ellipses with the Sun at one focus.
Kepler 2 : une planète va plus vite près: Kepler 2: a planet moves faster near the Sun.
Les astronautes de l'ISS flottent parce: Astronauts on the ISS float because they are constantly falling around the Earth, not because there is no gravity.
Les marées viennent surtout de la Lune,: Tides come mostly from the Moon, which pulls harder on the side of the Earth facing it.
À 400 km d'altitude, la gravité vaut enc: At 400 km altitude, gravity is still about 90% of what it is on the ground.
Orbite elliptique : A est le point le pl: Elliptical orbit: A is the point closest to the Sun, B the farthest
La Voie lactée, l'expansion de l'Univers: The Milky Way, the expansion of the Universe and its history.
La Voie lactée est une galaxie spirale d: The Milky Way is a spiral galaxy of about 100 to 400 billion stars.
Hubble (1929) : les galaxies s'éloignent: Hubble (1929): galaxies move away faster the farther they are. The Universe is expanding.
Big Bang : il y a 13,8 milliards d'année: Big Bang: 13.8 billion years ago, the Universe was very hot and dense; it is not an explosion in space.
Le fond diffus cosmologique est la lumiè: The cosmic microwave background is the light emitted 380,000 years after the Big Bang.
Le Big Bang n'a pas de centre : l'expans: The Big Bang has no center: expansion happens everywhere at once.
Constellations, saisons, télescopes et u: Constellations, seasons, telescopes and units of distance.
Les constellations sont des alignements: Constellations are apparent alignments: their stars are at very different distances.
Une année-lumière est une distance (≈ 9: A light-year is a distance (≈ 9,461 billion km), not a duration.
Un télescope sert surtout à collecter de: A telescope is mainly used to collect light: the bigger the mirror, the fainter what you can see.
Le ciel semble tourner autour de l'étoil: The sky seems to turn around the North Star because of the Earth's rotation.
Regarder loin, c'est regarder dans le pa: Looking far away means looking into the past: a star's light has sometimes traveled for thousands of years.
Fusées, satellites, missions habitées et: Rockets, satellites, crewed missions and deep space probes.
Gagarine (1961) : premier humain en orbi: Gagarin (1961): the first human in orbit; Apollo 11 (1969): the first step on the Moon.
Une fusée avance en éjectant des gaz ver: A rocket moves forward by ejecting gases backward (action-reaction): it doesn't need air to push against.
Voyager 1 a quitté l'héliosphère en 2012: Voyager 1 left the heliosphere in 2012; it is the most distant human-made object.
Dans l'espace, une fusée ne « s'appuie »: In space, a rocket doesn't “push” against anything: it's Newton's third law.
Détecter d'autres mondes et chercher la: Detecting other worlds and searching for life.
Première exoplanète autour d'une étoile: First exoplanet around a Sun-like star: 51 Pegasi b (Mayor and Queloz, 1995).

Zone habitable : la distance où l'eau po: Habitable zone: the distance at which water could be liquid on the surface.
Zone habitable ne veut pas dire habitée,: Habitable zone doesn't mean inhabited, or even habitable: Mars is in the Sun's by broad estimates, and it is a frozen desert.
Méthode des transits : l'éclat baisse qu: Transit method: the brightness drops when the planet passes
Ce qui manque dans l'Univers : la masse: What's missing from the Universe: the invisible mass and the acceleration.
Les galaxies tournent trop vite pour la: Galaxies spin too fast for their visible matter alone (Vera Rubin): mass is missing, dark matter.
Matière ordinaire ≈ 5 %, matière noire ≈: Ordinary matter ≈ 5%, dark matter ≈ 27%, dark energy ≈ 68% of the content of the Universe.
L'énergie noire accélère l'expansion de: Dark energy accelerates the expansion of the Universe (discovered in 1998 with supernovas).
La matière noire n'interagit pas avec la: Dark matter does not interact with light; it is detected by its gravity (gravitational lensing).
Matière noire ne veut pas dire trous noi: Dark matter doesn't mean black holes or dark clouds: those would be ordinary matter.
